{
  "action": "INVESTIGATE",
  "reason": "Round 0 with no findings, evidence, hypotheses, or tasks. The symptom is a request latency and error-rate observation window across gateway, backend, postgres, redis, and payment, and database_health_normal is false. No causal evidence exists yet, so the only valid action is to open targeted evidence collection. Two discriminating tasks are affordable within budget (24 tool calls, 32 LLM calls, round 0 of 6): one to localize the earliest metric divergence and dependency direction, and one to inspect change/config chronology before concluding anything.",
  "assignments": [
    {
      "task_id": "task-0001",
      "role": "metrics",
      "question": "Across gateway, backend, postgres, redis, and payment for the window starting 2026-10-01T12:00:00Z, which service shows the earliest divergence in request latency and error-rate metrics, and what is the dependency direction among these services?",
      "allowed_tools": [
        "query_metrics",
        "get_dependencies"
      ],
      "filters": {
        "start_ts": "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z",
        "end_ts": "2026-10-01T12:30:00Z",
        "services": [
          "gateway",
          "backend",
          "postgres",
          "redis",
          "payment"
        ],
        "metric_names": [
          "latency",
          "error_rate"
        ]
      },
      "reason": "No metric evidence has been collected yet; the earliest divergence and dependency direction are the minimal facts needed to distinguish an upstream gateway/backend problem from a downstream postgres/redis/payment problem without treating symptoms as the culprit.",
      "expected_discriminator": "The first service (by timestamp) whose latency and error_rate diverge from baseline, together with the dependency graph edge direction, shown to originate upstream of or at the earliest degrading node rather than only in the caller that surfaces the symptom."
    },
    {
      "task_id": "task-0002",
      "role": "changes",
      "question": "Were there any deployment, config, maintenance, or scaling changes affecting gateway, backend, postgres, redis, or payment around 2026-10-01T12:00:00Z, and does any change timestamp precede the onset of the observed latency and error-rate degradation?",
      "allowed_tools": [
        "query_changes",
        "get_config_diff"
      ],
      "filters": {
        "start_ts": "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z",
        "end_ts": "2026-10-01T12:30:00Z",
        "services": [
          "gateway",
          "backend",
          "postgres",
          "redis",
          "payment"
        ]
      },
      "reason": "Config diffs and change chronology must be inspected before concluding evidence is insufficient. A change coincident with the incident window is the most direct causal candidate and requires get_config_diff to establish an observed mechanism rather than an error string alone.",
      "expected_discriminator": "A concrete change record whose timestamp precedes the observed latency and error-rate degradation, plus a config diff showing a modification with an observable effect on the affected service; its absence supports ruling out change-induced causation."
    }
  ],
  "hypothesis_updates": [],
  "selected_hypothesis_id": null,
  "stop_reason": null
}
